name: Surfing Dog capability vocabulary
title: What an AI agent can do at a business
summary: The things an AI agent can do for a person at a business, from finding it to getting a refund. Each one has a definition, what has to be seen before anyone may say a business offers it, and how it is met through each kind of agent door. The ids never change: a capability is added, never renamed.

state_meanings.yes: An agent can do it through a door the business published.
state_meanings.partial: An agent can start it and a person has to finish it, it sits behind the customer's own account, or payment is only described.
state_meanings.no: Nothing the business published lets an agent do it.
state_meanings.na: It does not apply to this kind of business, like ordering at a dentist.

evidence_meanings.declared: The business's own site or door says so: its structured data, its pages, its manifest or its registration, or a door that meets it by what its protocol implies. Nobody has carried it out.
evidence_meanings.tested: A network's own read of the door, signed as its crawler, saw the door answer and list it (a tool, a skill, an operation or a kind of item) in the 7 days before. A read lists what a door offers and does nothing else: nobody has carried it out.
evidence_meanings.proven: Someone other than the business carried it out and signed what happened: a receipt the customer's agent counter-signed, or the signed reports of agent platforms a network recognises.

doors.label: Agent inbox
doors.how: The manifest at /.well-known/agent-inbox.json lists the kinds of request the inbox takes (item_types). Each kind meets the capabilities it carries: a booking meets book, and changing, cancelling and following it.

doors.label: MCP server
doors.how: A tool whose name says the action. A tool the server marks read-only, or one whose name only reads (get, list, search), meets only the capabilities that read.

doors.label: A2A agent
doors.how: Any agent card can be sent a message. A skill whose name says the action meets that capability too.

doors.label: OpenAPI
doors.how: An operation, by its method and path or its operationId. POST adds create, PUT and PATCH add update, DELETE adds delete. An operation by GET only reads.

doors.label: REST API
doors.how: An endpoint the business documents for agents, read as an OpenAPI operation is.

doors.label: UCP
doors.how: The capabilities a UCP profile names, by the last part of each name (dev.ucp.shopping.checkout is checkout): checkout means orders, catalog means a catalogue and stock, order means following an order, return means returns, and payment handlers mean payment.

doors.label: ACP
doors.how: Checkout means orders. Delegated payment (delegated_payment) means payment.

doors.label: WebMCP
doors.how: A tool a web page registers for the browser's agent, read as an MCP tool is. Experimental: it counts toward a score and never toward a readiness level.

never_doors: An email address, a phone number, a text or chat-app link, a web form or a page written for people never meets a capability. A person can use them; an agent cannot rely on them.
names: A tool, skill or operation name is split into words (create_booking and createBooking are the same two words). The action and its object must both be there, each in its own word: book alone, or create with booking. Words that name something else rule it out: a tool that cancels a cart is not cancelling an order.

capabilities.label: Find
capabilities.question: Can an agent read who the business is, its opening hours and where it is?
capabilities.definition: Read who the business is, where it is or which area it serves, and when it is open, as data.
capabilities.partial: Only part of it is data, such as a name and an address with no hours.

evidence.declared: schema.org data on the business's own site (LocalBusiness or one of its types, with an address or opening hours), or a tool, skill or operation that reads the business's details.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list a tool, skill or operation that reads the business's details.
evidence.proven: Signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that such a read answered.

not_enough: Hours or an address that are only in the text of a page, or in an image.

capabilities.label: Catalogue
capabilities.question: Can an agent read its services, products or menu, with prices?
capabilities.definition: Read what the business sells or offers, with prices: its products, its services or its menu.
capabilities.partial: Items without prices, or prices only behind the customer's account.

evidence.declared: schema.org Product, Offer, Menu or Service data with prices on the business's own site, a product feed, a UCP or ACP catalogue with items in it, or a tool, skill or operation that lists products, services or a menu.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list a tool, skill or operation that lists them.
evidence.proven: Signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that such a listing answered.

not_enough: A menu or price list that is only a PDF or an image.
A commerce profile that names a catalogue and lists nothing the business sells.

capabilities.label: Availability
capabilities.question: Can an agent check free slots or stock?
capabilities.definition: Check what is free before asking for it: open times for a booking, rooms or seats, or whether something is in stock.
capabilities.partial: Only behind the customer's own account.

evidence.declared: A tool, skill or operation that checks free times or stock, an agent inbox that takes bookings, or a UCP catalogue with stock.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: Signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that a check answered with times or stock.

not_enough: A calendar shown as a picture or a widget for people.

capabilities.label: Message
capabilities.question: Can an agent send the business a message and get an answer?
capabilities.definition: Send the business a question or a request in words and get an answer back through the same door, before buying or after it.
capabilities.partial: The message goes in and no answer can come back through the door.

evidence.declared: An agent inbox that takes messages, an A2A agent card, or a tool, skill or operation that sends the business a message or opens a support request.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: Signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that a message was taken, and the business's answer reached them.

not_enough: An email address, a phone number, a chat-app link or a contact form for people.
A chat widget that only a person in a browser can use.

capabilities.label: Negotiate
capabilities.question: Can an agent ask for a quote, make an offer or get a counter-offer?
capabilities.definition: Ask for a quote, and answer one: accept it, decline it or propose something else, such as another time or another price.
capabilities.partial: A quote can be asked for and the answer comes only by email or phone.

evidence.declared: An agent inbox that takes quote requests, or a tool, skill or operation that asks for a quote or answers an offer.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: Signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that a quote request was taken and answered.

not_enough: A price calculator that only shows a number and takes no request.

capabilities.label: Book
capabilities.question: Can an agent make a booking, with its details?
capabilities.definition: Make a booking for a person (a time, a table, a room, a seat or an appointment) with the details it needs, and get back that it is booked or requested, with a reference.
capabilities.partial: The agent can only fill in a booking that a person completes, or only behind the customer's own account.

evidence.declared: An agent inbox that takes bookings, or a tool, skill or operation that makes a booking.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: A signed receipt of a confirmed booking that the customer's agent counter-signed, or signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that a booking was made.

not_enough: A booking page or a booking widget for people.
A tool that only lists free times: that is availability.

capabilities.label: Order
capabilities.question: Can an agent place an order, with its options?
capabilities.definition: Place an order for goods or food with its options and quantities, and get back that it is placed or accepted, with a reference.
capabilities.partial: The agent can fill a basket and hand a link to a person who completes the order.

evidence.declared: An agent inbox that takes orders, a UCP or ACP checkout, or a tool, skill or operation that places an order, together with something the business really sells: products or offers with prices on its own site, or a cart that works.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: A signed receipt of an accepted or paid order that the customer's agent counter-signed, or signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that an order was placed.

not_enough: A commerce platform's profile that every site on that platform gets, on a site with no prices and no cart.
A tool that changes, cancels or returns an order that exists: that is change, cancel or return.

capabilities.label: Sign up
capabilities.question: Can an agent sign the person up: an account, a membership, a class, a course or a newsletter list for the business's own service?
capabilities.definition: Sign the person up for the business's own service: an account, a membership, a class, a course or a newsletter.
capabilities.partial: The agent can start a sign-up that a person finishes.

evidence.declared: A tool, skill or operation that signs a person up, or a schema.org RegisterAction or JoinAction.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: Signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that a sign-up went through.

not_enough: Signing in, or anything that only logs a person in.
Registering a tool, a webhook, a key or a device, or adding staff.

capabilities.label: Pay
capabilities.question: Can an agent pay, and is it clear how payment happens?
capabilities.definition: Pay for a booking or an order, or learn exactly how payment happens: on the spot, through a payment the agent can make, or through a link a person completes.
capabilities.partial: How to pay is described and a person has to pay.

evidence.declared: UCP payment handlers, ACP delegated payment, or a tool, skill or operation that takes a payment.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: A signed receipt of a paid order or booking that the customer's agent counter-signed.

not_enough: Card logos or a payment page for people.

capabilities.label: Change
capabilities.question: Can an agent change a booking or an order?
capabilities.definition: Change a booking or an order that exists: another time, another size, another address. A request to change that comes back with a reference the agent can follow counts the same as a change made at once.
capabilities.partial: Only behind the customer's own account.

evidence.declared: An agent inbox that takes bookings or orders, or a tool, skill or operation that changes or reschedules one.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: A signed receipt of an agreed change (an amended receipt), or signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that a change went through.

not_enough: Changing a cart before it is an order.

capabilities.label: Cancel
capabilities.question: Can an agent cancel a booking or an order?
capabilities.definition: Cancel a booking or an order that exists. A request to cancel that comes back with a reference the agent can follow counts the same as cancelling at once.
capabilities.partial: Only behind the customer's own account.

evidence.declared: An agent inbox that takes bookings or orders, or a tool, skill or operation that cancels one.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: A signed receipt of the cancellation's outcome, or signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that a cancellation went through.

not_enough: Cancelling a cart, a basket or a checkout.
A cancellation policy: that is policies.

capabilities.label: Track
capabilities.question: Can an agent see the status of a booking, an order or a delivery?
capabilities.definition: Follow a booking, an order or a delivery: whether it is confirmed, where it is, when it arrives.
capabilities.partial: Only behind the customer's own account.

evidence.declared: An agent inbox that takes bookings or orders, a UCP order capability, or a tool, skill or operation that reads a status.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: Signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that a status read answered.

not_enough: A tracking page a person opens from an email.

capabilities.label: Return or refund
capabilities.question: Can an agent start a return, a refund or an exchange?
capabilities.definition: Start a return, a refund or an exchange. A request that comes back with a reference the agent can follow counts the same as a refund made at once.
capabilities.partial: Only behind the customer's own account.

evidence.declared: An agent inbox that takes refunds, a UCP return capability, or a tool, skill or operation that starts a return or a refund.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: A signed receipt of the refund's promise or its outcome, or signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that a return was started.

not_enough: A returns policy: that is policies.

capabilities.label: Receipt
capabilities.question: Can an agent get a receipt or an invoice?
capabilities.definition: Get a receipt or an invoice for what was booked, ordered or paid.
capabilities.partial: Only behind the customer's own account, or only by email.

evidence.declared: An agent inbox that takes orders (it gives signed receipts), or a tool, skill or operation that returns a receipt or an invoice.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: A signed receipt the customer's agent counter-signed.

not_enough: A receipt only sent to a person's email.

capabilities.label: Feedback
capabilities.question: Can an agent leave feedback or a review?
capabilities.definition: Leave feedback or a review with the business itself.
capabilities.partial: Only behind the customer's own account.

evidence.declared: A tool, skill or operation that leaves feedback or a review.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: Signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that feedback was taken.

not_enough: A link to a review site run by someone else.

capabilities.label: Membership
capabilities.question: Can an agent pause, resume or end a membership or subscription?
capabilities.definition: Manage a membership or a subscription that exists: pause it, resume it, change the plan or end it.
capabilities.partial: Only behind the customer's own account.

evidence.declared: A tool, skill or operation that pauses, resumes, changes or ends a membership or subscription.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: Signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that the change went through.

not_enough: A page that says to email the business to cancel.

capabilities.label: Vouchers
capabilities.question: Can an agent use a gift card, a voucher or loyalty points?
capabilities.definition: Use or check a gift card, a voucher, a promotion code or loyalty points.
capabilities.partial: Only behind the customer's own account.

evidence.declared: A tool, skill or operation that redeems or checks a voucher, a gift card or points.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: Signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that a voucher was taken.

not_enough: A promotion code printed on a page.

capabilities.label: Waitlist
capabilities.question: Can an agent join a waitlist?
capabilities.definition: Join a waitlist for a time, a table, a class or a product, and leave it.
capabilities.partial: Only behind the customer's own account.

evidence.declared: A tool, skill or operation that joins a waitlist.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: Signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that a place on the list was taken.

not_enough: A form for people to leave their email.

capabilities.label: Support
capabilities.question: Can an agent raise a complaint or a problem with an order?
capabilities.definition: Raise a complaint or a problem with a booking or an order, and follow it.
capabilities.partial: A problem can be raised and nothing comes back through the door.

evidence.declared: An agent inbox that takes messages, or a tool, skill or operation that opens a support ticket or a complaint.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: Signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that a ticket was opened and answered.

not_enough: A help centre of articles for people.

capabilities.label: Policies
capabilities.question: Can an agent read the cancellation, return, deposit or no-show policy?
capabilities.definition: Read the terms that matter before and after: cancellation, returns, deposits, no-shows and delivery.
capabilities.partial: The policy is on a page an agent can read and not as data or through a door.

evidence.declared: schema.org MerchantReturnPolicy or similar data, a policy in the inbox's terms, or a tool, skill or operation that reads a policy.
evidence.tested: A network's read of the door saw it answer and list it.
evidence.proven: Signed reports from agent platforms a network recognises, saying that the policy read answered.

not_enough: A policy only in a PDF.

changelog.summary: Twenty capabilities in five parts of a customer's journey, each with a label and a question, the states yes, partial, no and na, and the evidence ladder declared, tested, proven.
Tested is produced: a network's own read of a door that saw it answer and list a capability in the 7 days before.

Each capability now has a definition, other words for it, what partial means for it, what has to be seen at each step of the evidence ladder, what is not enough, and how each kind of agent door meets it, with example names. Message, negotiate, book, order and pay name the kind of request a directory filters by (ask, quote, book, order, pay). The door kinds, what never counts as a door and how names are read are written down. Order needs something the business really sells: a commerce platform's profile that every site on it gets is not enough on its own. No capability was added, renamed or removed: every id, label and question is as in version 1.
